findings.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:4027` checks restricted-priv only against the raw `item` name/`item.Priv.String()`, but `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:4054` expands `mysql.AllPriv` into `allPrivs` and `break`s without re-checking restrictions for the expanded set (same pattern in REVOKE at `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3951` and `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3967`). `pkg/parser/mysql/privs.go:314` shows `mysql.AllGlobalPrivs` includes static privs like `DropPriv` and `FilePriv`, so `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES` can include restricted static privileges. `pkg/util/sem/v2/sem.go:186` shows restriction is an exact prefix/map check, so "ALL PRIVILEGES" being unrestricted does not imply individual restricted privs are gated.
findings.fix: In `collectVisitInfoFromGrantStmt`/`collectVisitInfoFromRevokeStmt`, when `item.Priv == mysql.AllPriv`, expand `allPrivs` first and enforce `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN` if **any** expanded privilege is restricted (e.g. `if semv2.IsRestrictedPrivilege(strings.ToUpper(priv.String())) { append RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN visitInfo; break }`). Apply the same logic for DB/table-level ALL expansions.
findings.impact: SEMv2’s intended “restricted privilege delegation requires `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN`” can be bypassed by using `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES`/`REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES` unless operators also remember to restrict "ALL PRIVILEGES" in config. This undermines privilege-limiting policy and can allow delegating restricted static privileges without `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN` in clusters relying on SEMv2 for security controls.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `collectVisitInfoFromGrantStmt` still expands `mysql.AllPriv` without checking restrictions on the expanded privileges (see `upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go` around the function body starting near line ~3843).
findings.verify: Add a unit test extending `pkg/privilege/privileges/privileges_test.go:2226` (`TestGrantOptionWithSEMv2`): enable SEMv2, mark e.g. `DROP` (or `FILE`) restricted, create a user that has **all** required static privileges + `GRANT OPTION` but not `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN`, then assert `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* TO grantee` fails with `[planner:1227] ... RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN ...`. Add a similar `REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES` case if revoke is also intended to be gated.
findings.what: SEMv2 restricted-privilege gating via `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN` is bypassable with `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES` / `REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES`: the code only checks whether the literal "ALL PRIVILEGES" token is restricted, and never enforces `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN` based on the expanded privilege set that includes restricted static privileges (e.g. `DROP`, `FILE`).

subject: sem, privilege: fix the issue that some privileges cannot be limited (#64160)
summary: The commit fixes case-sensitivity in SEMv2 restricted-privilege checks for GRANT/REVOKE by uppercasing privilege names and adds uppercase assertions in SEM helpers/tests. A remaining High-severity gap is that `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES` / `REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES` can bypass the `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN` gate for restricted static privileges because restrictions aren’t evaluated against the expanded ALL privilege set.
